title: Why You Should Never Eat Polar Bear Liver
description:
Over 400 years ago, Dutch sailors stuck in the Arctic cooked a polar bear's liver. Days later they fell sick and their skin began to peel. The reason: vitamin A. It piles up the food chain, from fish to seals to bears, and just one gram of polar bear liver holds more than an adult's limit for a whole day.

Would you have known?

Sources: Gerrit de Veer's journal of Barents' third voyage (1597); Rodahl & Moore, "The vitamin A content and toxicity of bear and seal liver", Biochemical Journal 37, 166 (1943); NIH Office of Dietary Supplements, Vitamin A fact sheet; Rodahl, Norsk Polarinstitutt Skrifter 95 (1949).
Animation and music: TrueWhys (original).
TrueWhys — the real story behind life's weirdest whys.
